name: Praxilla of Sicyon
bio: Praxilla of Sicyon was a lyric poetess of the middle of the fifth century BC, counted by the ancients among the canonical women poets of Greece. She wrote hymns and dithyrambs and drinking-songs, and a metre was named after her, the Praxillean.

She is remembered above all for her hymn on Adonis, in which the dying youth, asked in the underworld what he most regrets leaving above, names the sun, the moon, the stars, and then cucumbers, apples and pears. The reply was ridiculed, and gave rise to the proverb 'sillier than Praxilla's Adonis'. Only a handful of lines survive.

poems.title: Fragment 1: Ἀλλὰ τεὸν οὔποτε θυμὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἔπειθον
poems.author: Praxilla of Sicyon
poems.text: Ἀλλὰ τεὸν οὔποτε θυμὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἔπειθον.

poems.title: Fragment 2: Κάλλιστον μὲν ἐγὼ λείπω φάος ἠελίοιο
poems.author: Praxilla of Sicyon
poems.text:
Κάλλιστον μὲν ἐγὼ λείπω φάος ἠελίοιο,
δεύτερον ἄστρα φαεινὰ σεληναίης τε πρόσωπον
ἠδὲ καὶ ὡραίους σικύους καὶ μῆλα καὶ ὄγχνας.

poems.title: Fragment 3: Ἀδμήτου λόγον, ὦ ʼταῖρε, μαθὼν τοὺς ἀγαθοὺς φίλει
poems.author: Praxilla of Sicyon
poems.text:
Ἀδμήτου λόγον, ὦ ʼταῖρε, μαθὼν τοὺς ἀγαθοὺς φίλει·
τῶν δειλῶν δʼ ἀπέχου, γνοὺς ὅτι δειλοῖς ὀλίγα χάρις.

poems.title: Fragment 4: Ὑπὸ παντὶ λίθῳ σκορπίος
poems.author: Praxilla of Sicyon
poems.text:
Ὑπὸ παντὶ λίθῳ σκορπίος, ὦ ʼταῖρʼ, ὑποδύεται·
φράζευ, μή σε βάλῃ· τῷ δʼ ἀφανεῖ πᾶς ἕπεται δόλος.

poems.title: Fragment 5: Ὦ διὰ τῶν θυρίδων καλὸν ἐμβλέπουσα
poems.author: Praxilla of Sicyon
poems.text:
Ὦ διὰ τῶν θυρίδων καλὸν ἐμβλέπουσα,
παρθένε, τὰν κεφαλάν, τὰ δʼ ἔνερθε νύμφα.

poems.title: Fragment 1 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Praxilla of Sicyon
poems.text: But they never persuaded the heart that is in thy breast.

poems.title: Fragment 2 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Praxilla of Sicyon
poems.text: The fairest thing I leave is the sunlight, and fairest after that the shining stars and the face of the moon, aye and ripe cucumbers and apples and pears.

poems.title: Fragment 3 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Praxilla of Sicyon
poems.text: Learn the tale of Admetus, my friend, and seek acquaintance of the brave; but from the coward hold thee aloof, since there's little gratitude in such as he.

poems.title: Fragment 4 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Praxilla of Sicyon
poems.note: Edmonds numbers this fragment 4; his Greek is the one-line form.
poems.text: Under every stone, my friend, beware of a scorpion.

poems.title: Fragment 5 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Praxilla of Sicyon
poems.text: O you that look so prettily at me through the window, a maiden in face but a wedded bride below.
